title: KOSPI Close November 25, 2026: Falls 6.16% to 4,697.51, KOSDAQ -2.29%
content:
KOSPI closed at 4,697.51, down 6.16%, giving up the 5,000 level it regained a day earlier, and KOSDAQ closed at 650.64, down 2.29%, as a sell-off in U.S. tech stocks hit Korean chip heavyweights. A sell sidecar was triggered on KOSPI, while security, cosmetics, game and content stocks and Hanjin KAL rose against the market.

Our read: three sessions, three moves of more than 3%

KOSPI has now moved -3.31%, +6.32% and -6.16% in three straight sessions, and today's close of 4,697.51 is below the Nov 23 close of 4,708.54, so the whole Nov 24 rebound has been erased. The damage was concentrated: the four chip-related large caps in the table below each fell about 10% to 12%, far more than the index, while KOSDAQ, where those names carry less weight, fell 2.29%. Foreigners net sold about 1.9 trillion won on KOSPI one day after their first net buying in eight sessions, and individuals absorbed about 1.42 trillion won of it. Four stocks in unrelated themes (AhnLab, Fasoo AI, TPC Robotics, Beauty Skin) still closed at the daily limit, which shows money rotating within the market rather than leaving every sector.

1. Chip large caps lead the fall

KOSPI opened at 4,809.00 (-3.94%) and fell as low as 4,672.55 (-6.66%) before closing at 4,697.51. KOSDAQ opened at 654.21 (-1.75%), touched 641.08 (-3.72%) and closed at 650.64.

Korean market coverage attributed the fall to an overnight drop in U.S. tech stocks, citing doubts about returns on AI investment, forecasts of a memory chip oversupply and an accounting probe involving Nvidia. A higher won-dollar exchange rate was also cited as a burden. These points come from market coverage and were not independently confirmed.

On KOSPI, foreigners net sold about 1.9 trillion won and individuals net bought about 1.42 trillion won (provisional). On KOSDAQ, institutions net bought about 27 billion won and individuals net sold about 35 billion won.

2. Cybersecurity — reported hack of U.S. intelligence agencies

Korean coverage cited a New York Times report that the CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence were hacked and some unclassified information was exposed. Security stocks rose on expectations of higher government and corporate security spending; AhnLab and Fasoo AI hit the upper limit. The report was not independently confirmed here, and a theme-driven move is not the same as new orders or earnings.

3. Robots and actuators — TPC Robotics supply deal

TPC Robotics hit the upper limit on reports that it signed a contract to supply motors and electric actuators to a chip equipment maker that works with Samsung Electronics. The contract was not independently confirmed.

4. Cosmetics — Korea-China FTA follow-up talks and exports

Cosmetics stocks rose on reports that follow-up negotiations on services and investment under the Korea-China FTA were substantially concluded, along with year-end shopping season hopes and export growth in the U.S., Europe and Latin America. Formal signing and ratification steps remain.

6. Hanjin KAL — control dispute

Korean coverage said Hoban Construction became the largest shareholder of Hanjin KAL on Nov 4 and that Chairman Cho Won-tae's side signaled further share purchases, reviving the control contest. Preferred shares and airline affiliates rose; Hanjin KAL preferred shares have a small float and can be volatile. The shareholding details were not independently confirmed.

Quick FAQ

How did KOSPI and KOSDAQ close on Nov 25?
KOSPI closed at 4,697.51 (-6.16%), back below 5,000 and 4,700, and KOSDAQ at 650.64 (-2.29%).

Why did Korean stocks fall?
A reported sell-off in U.S. tech stocks hit chip large caps, and foreigners net sold about 1.9 trillion won on KOSPI.

Which stocks hit the upper limit?
AhnLab, Fasoo AI, TPC Robotics and Beauty Skin closed near +30%.

This brief is our own summary based on same-day Korean market coverage and Daum Finance closing data; it is not a translation and not investment advice. See our Disclaimer and evidence labels.
